name: Creative Snap
description: Thanos wants to destroy the avengers base, but he needs to destroy the avengers along with their base. Let we represent their base with an array, where each position can be occupied by many avengers, but one avenger can occupy only one position. Length of their base is a perfect power of $$$2$$$. Thanos wants to destroy the base using minimum power. He starts with the whole base and in one step he can do either of following: if the current length is at least $$$2$$$, divide the base into $$$2$$$ equal halves and destroy them separately, or burn the current base. If it contains no avenger in it, it takes $$$A$$$ amount of power, otherwise it takes his $$$B \cdot n_a \cdot l$$$ amount of power, where $$$n_a$$$ is the number of avengers and $$$l$$$ is the length of the current base. Output the minimum power needed by Thanos to destroy the avengers' base.
input_specification: The first line contains four integers $$$n$$$, $$$k$$$, $$$A$$$ and $$$B$$$ ($$$1 \leq n \leq 30$$$, $$$1 \leq k \leq 10^5$$$, $$$1 \leq A,B \leq 10^4$$$), where $$$2^n$$$ is the length of the base, $$$k$$$ is the number of avengers and $$$A$$$ and $$$B$$$ are the constants explained in the question. The second line contains $$$k$$$ integers $$$a_{1}, a_{2}, a_{3}, \ldots, a_{k}$$$ ($$$1 \leq a_{i} \leq 2^n$$$), where $$$a_{i}$$$ represents the position of avenger in the base.
output_specification: Output one integer — the minimum power needed to destroy the avengers base.
approach_summary: Verify predicate monotonicity: P(x) is true for x ≤ K and false otherwise. Binary search over the answer domain to find the boundary in O(log(Range) × Verify_Time).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1111C — Creative Snap [33. Binary Search]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary search on the monotonic answer domain.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The predicate function $P(x)$ ('Is answer $\le x$ feasible?') is monotonic: if $P(x)$ is true for some value, it remains true for all larger values (or vice versa). This allows binary division of the answer search space $[\text{low}, \text{high}]$ in $O(\log(\text{Range}))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N \log(\text{Range}))$
  The binary search divides the search interval by 2 at each iteration, requiring $\log_2(\text{Range})$ steps. In each step, the feasibility check `check(mid)` scans the array in $\mathcal{O}(N)$ time.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(1)$ auxiliary space
  The algorithm operates directly over the input array without allocating extra auxiliary memory.
